sanskrit_verse:
ब्राह्मणस्वर्णहारी तु राज्ञे मुसलमर्पयेत् ।
स्वकर्म व्याख्यायंस् तेन हतो मुक्तोऽपि वाशुचिः ॥२५७॥
transliteration: brāhmaṇasvarṇahārī tu rājñe musalam arpayet | svakarma vyākhyāyaṃs tena hato mukto 'pi vāśuciḥ || 257 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who steals gold from a Brāhmaṇa shall offer a pestle to the king. Having explained his act fully, he becomes ritually pure even if physically harmed or released.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: The king holds executive capacity to receive restitution.
Causation: Ritual purity is restored through complete disclosure and action alignment.
Capacity-based responsibility: Purity depends on inner transparency, not external condition.
Restoration logic: Harm or release does not determine spiritual status; truthfulness does.
Consciousness alignment: Purity arises from self-revelation and surrender to dharma.
executable_legal_axioms: IF full_disclosure_of_act EXISTS THEN ritual_purity = TRUE regardless_of_physical_state
IF physical_harm_occurs AND truth_is_expressed THEN no_impurity_attached
IF release_by_authority AND self_revelation_complete THEN purification_acknowledged
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, the threshold for spiritual rehabilitation lies in total factual disclosure rather than punitive outcome. Authority resides with the sovereign to accept symbolic restitution. Physical consequences do not negate ontological cleansing when consciousness is aligned with dharma.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that ritual impurity dissolves upon truthful exposition of the act. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential revelation leading to purification. Proportional responsibility aligns with integrity-restoring action, not infliction. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that consciousness, once purified, renders all prior states irrelevant.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: Full verbal and written disclosure of the theft before lawful authority.
Responsibility assumption protocol: Voluntary offering of a musala as symbolic restitution.
Capacity restoration: Reintegration into ritual life contingent upon truth-speaking.
Integrity reintegration: Acknowledgment by community elder or priest after disclosure.
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law executes the will of Sanātana Dharma. The thief is cleansed not by punishment but by revelation. The king receives the symbol; consciousness restores the soul. There is no punishment—only alignment. Dharma is restored. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
